description: baseline

Bottleneck: trailing-update GEMMs run on SIMT FP32 cores (cutlass3x_sm100_simt_sgemm), leaving TF32 tensor cores (~500 TFLOP/s) idle. Implement blocked Householder QR from scratch: factor a b-column panel (b=32/64), form the compact-WY T factor, apply the block reflector to the trailing matrix via cuBLAS GEMM with CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH. Maximize the tensor-core trailing fraction; produce native H/tau. Sweep block size.

Blocked Householder QR from scratch in PyTorch (panel=sequential Householder, compact-WY T, trailing update via batched einsum/bmm) with global TF32 enabled, b=64. Algorithm structurally correct: 17/19 test shapes pass incl all dense 512/1024/2048/4096. band (scaled=28.2) and rowscale (scaled=25.7) fail factor_rtol=20 by a hair - pure TF32 precision shortfall on wide-dynamic-range cases. Next: fix precision.

Blocked Householder QR in PyTorch, FP32 (TF32 off), b=64. PASSES ALL validation (algorithm numerically sound). Geomean 98230us (2.2x worse than baseline 44724). KEY FINDING: shape3 (b640,n512) is 9.3x FASTER (1075141->115009us) via batched-GEMM trailing update - confirms the brief's thesis. But Python-loop panel factorization (b sequential launches/panel) destroys small-batch/large-n: shape6 (b2,n4096) 15x worse, shape0 (n32) 16x worse. Fix: custom-CUDA batched panel kernel + cuBLAS TF32 strided-batched trailing GEMM.

First custom-CUDA: batched panel_factor_kernel (one CTA/matrix, warp-cooperative Householder) + form_T_kernel + torch.bmm TF32 trailing update, b=64. Builds OK but produces NaN/Inf and huge residuals on ALL shapes - bug in custom kernel(s). Next: isolate via standalone test vs torch.geqrf.

Fixed the panel_factor_kernel head double-count bug (unit-head term was added by all 32 lanes before warp reduction; now lane-0 only). Custom-CUDA panel+T now NUMERICALLY CORRECT: 17/19 test shapes pass with identical residuals to the FP32 PyTorch reference (iter1). Only band (scaled=28.2) and rowscale (scaled=25.6) fail factor_rtol=20 - pure TF32-trailing-GEMM precision on wide-dynamic-range cases. All 7 benchmark shapes are well-conditioned dense and pass easily. Next: 3xTF32 split-precision trailing GEMM for FP32 accuracy on tensor cores.

3xTF32 split-precision trailing GEMM (split FP32 into TF32 hi+lo, 3 tensor-core bmms capture cross terms). PASSES ALL 19 validation shapes (band/rowscale residuals 28->0.03). Geomean 29913us = 1.50x speedup vs baseline 44724. Per-shape vs baseline: n32 2.6x, n176 6.8x, n352 4.4x, n512(shape3) 12.2x, n1024 2.6x FASTER; but n2048 4.9x and n4096 30x SLOWER (one-CTA-per-matrix panel kernel underutilizes GPU at batch=2/8 with huge columns + 3x GEMM cost). Next: multi-CTA panel or hybrid for large-n/small-batch.

CRITICAL FINDING: GPU MODE leaderboard rejects any submission whose source contains the substring 'stream' (naive text scan in kernelbot api_utils.py: if 'stream' in submission_code.lower()). My getCurrentCUDAStream() triggered it. Removed explicit stream -> kernels launch on legacy NULL stream. PASSES ALL 19 validation. Geomean 33390us = 1.34x vs baseline. SUBMITTABLE (no stream substring, single stream). vs unsubmittable torch.bmm 29913us. Regressions remain at n2048(4.9x)/n4096(30x) from 1-CTA-per-matrix panel at small batch. Next: profile + fix small-batch panel + cut gather/scatter overhead.

PASSES ALL 19 validation. Geomean 33390us = 1.34x vs baseline (vs 29913 for the torch.bmm version, but THAT is unsubmittable due to 'stream' text scan; this one is SUBMITTABLE). Next: profile, then fix small-batch panel + reduce overhead.

PROFILE (nsys shape3 b640n512, commit 5e239a2): my TF32 trailing GEMM is already FAST (tensorop_tf32gemm only ~1-2% of GPU time - tensor cores working as intended). The bottleneck is now my PANEL: panel_factor_kernel ~26% + form_T_kernel ~5% (the sequential latency-bound parts), both doing per-step GLOBAL memory round-trips. (The big SIMT-sgemm/larft/orgqr/lacpy in the profile are the eval correctness-check's householder_product, not my kernel.) CONCLUSION: blocked structure succeeded - moved bulk to tensor cores; panel is now critical path. Next: shared-memory panel kernel (cache b cols in smem, all Householder steps in smem, write back once) - panel m*b*4<=128KB fits B200 smem for n<=512. Same metric 33390us (profile-only checkpoint).

Shared-memory panel kernel (cache m*b panel in dynamic smem, all Householder steps in smem). Build OK but launch fails with CUDA invalid argument (async) - the dynamic-smem opt-in (cudaFuncSetAttribute MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) isn't taking effect for the 128KB n=512 first panel. Next: verify smem_max query + SetAttribute return code, cap to safe limit.

Shared-memory panel kernel: load m*b panel into dynamic smem (opt-in size probed via cudaFuncSetAttribute loop), run all b Householder steps in smem (no per-step global traffic), write back once. Falls back to global-mem panel when m*b*4 > smem_limit (~227KB). PASSES ALL validation. Geomean 29686us = 1.51x (was 33390). Improved n176 (3067->2607), n352 (11655->9260), n1024 (92232->79182). shape3 flat (86629). n2048/4096 still regress (panel>smem, global fallback + tiny batch underutilization). This is the new submittable best. Next: attack n2048/4096 - tile the smem panel or multi-CTA, or accept hybrid.

PASSES ALL validation. Geomean 14692us = 3.04x vs baseline 44724! Per-shape: n32 212, n176 2609, n352 9277, n512(shape3) 86527, n1024 79192 (all MINE); n2048 77003, n4096 54362 (geqrf). Block-size sweep (brief asks for this). b=56 optimal: geomean 10757us = 4.16x baseline (was 14692 at b=64). Root cause: shared-memory panel occupancy cliff at n=512 - panel smem = 512*b*4 bytes; b<=56 -> 112KB -> 2 CTAs/SM resident, b=64 -> 128KB -> only 1 CTA/SM. form_T now via batched tensor-core GEMM: profile showed form_T_kernel (O(b^2*m) sequential dots) was ~as costly as the panel. Replaced with S=V^T V (batched 3xTF32 GEMM, tensor cores) + form_T_from_S recurrence (O(b^2) per matrix, no m-loop). Also set b=52 (best: 2 CTAs/SM safely, b52=9852 vs b56=10757). Now shapes5/6 (geqrf fallback) dominate. New submittable best. Next: beat geqrf on n2048/4096 to drop fallback.

In-place trailing update: generalized mm3->mm3g with per-operand leading-dim/stride; the final C-=V*Y GEMM (alpha=-1,beta0=+1, 3xTF32) writes directly into H's strided trailing block (ldR=n,sR=n*n), eliminating Dbuf, sub_kernel, scatter_C (gather_C kept so C is packed for W=V^T C). Cache cuBLAS handle + smem opt-in as function-static (created once, reused). cublasCreate costs tens of ms; recreating per custom_kernel call was real overhead, especially on small shapes where the eval runs many benchmark repeats. PASSES ALL validation. Geomean 6335us = 7.06x! shape0 213->121, shape1 1093->969, shape2 2524->2337, shape3 21354->21169, shape4 17015->16888. Added QR_FALLBACK flag and measured my-kernel-without-fallback to quantify the geqrf gap at large-n/small-batch: n2048(b8)=159911us vs geqrf 76779 (2.1x behind), n4096(b2)=747193us vs geqrf 54342 (13.8x behind). Geomean without fallback=9468 vs 6335 with -> fallback is correct. Root cause is GPU underutilization (2-8 CTAs in one-CTA-per-matrix panel); beating geqrf needs a multi-CTA cooperative-grid panel whose ~12000 grid-syncs for n4096 would likely cost more than geqrf's 27ms/matrix. LEADERBOARD: iter14 (6335us/7.06x) submitted SUCCESSFULLY (cached-handle fix resolved the 300s remote timeout; remote benchmark matches local). Metric unchanged 6335.

Tested reduced-precision trailing GEMM (QR_PREC flag, 1/2/3 TF32 passes) to cut the split+GEMM cost. RESULT: 3xTF32 is the minimum for validation. prec=1 (single TF32) fails band(scaled 33.5)/rowscale(26.9) > threshold 20. prec=2 (Ahi*Bhi+Ahi*Blo, asymmetric) is WORSE (band 46.1, rowscale 40.3, also test.1/test.7 fail) - dropping the Alo*Bhi cross term biases the result more than symmetric rounding. So 3xTF32 stays. Default unchanged (prec=3), metric 6335us. The split overhead is irreducible given the loose-but-real FP32 tolerance on wide-dynamic-range cases.

Swept smem-panel warps/CTA (QR_WARPS, instantiated <4>/<8>/<16>). 16 warps (512 threads/CTA) optimal: the per-Householder-step reductions over m rows finish in fewer passes. PASSES ALL validation. Geomean 5662us = 7.90x! Improves every blocked-QR shape: shape0 121->70, shape1 969->861, shape2 2337->2205, shape3(n512) 21169->20498, shape4(n1024) 16888->16316. shapes5/6 geqrf unchanged. New best, default now warps=16. Testing warps=32 next.

Completed warp sweep: 16 warps optimal. warps=32 (1024 threads/CTA) gives 5717us, marginally WORSE than 16 (5662) - 1024 threads forces 1 CTA/SM (occupancy loss) which outweighs faster reductions; shape3 20498->21082. Default warps=16 confirmed. Metric 5662us=7.90x (best). Submitting this.

Adaptive per-panel block: C++ caps b per panel so the m*b panel fits opt-in smem (floor 8), keeping the fast shared-memory panel path even for tall panels at n=2048 (first panels use b~27, later panels grow as m shrinks); loop now steps by the actual b. Lowered geqrf fallback threshold to n>=4096. PASSES ALL validation. Geomean 5121us = 8.73x! shape5(n2048,b8) 76779(geqrf)->38344(my smem panel, 2x). shape6(n4096,b2) stays geqrf 54431 (2-CTA underutilization beats my 133461). Per-shape: 70/861/2203/20507/16313/38344/54431. New best, leaderboard-pending. Now shape6(geqrf) + shapes3/4 are top contributors.

WHAT WORKED: (1) batched TF32 trailing GEMM is the core win - tensor cores carry the bulk, confirmed ~5% of GPU time; (2) form_T via GEMM (was O(b^2*m) sequential, ~as costly as panel); (3) smem panel + b=52 (occupancy cliff: b<=52 -> 2 CTAs/SM, b=64 -> 1); (4) 16 warps; (5) adaptive block extended the smem panel to n=2048, beating geqrf there (76.8->38.3ms). TWO CRITICAL FINDINGS FOR THE FLEET: (a) the GPU MODE leaderboard REJECTS any submission whose SOURCE TEXT contains the substring 'stream' (naive scan in kernelbot api_utils.py) - so getCurrentCUDAStream/cudaStream_t/cublasSetStream/torch.cuda.stream all fail; I use a private cublas handle on the default queue with no explicit stream arg. Worker6's multi-stream cuSOLVER (4.66x) WILL be rejected. (b) Per-call cublasCreate inflated REMOTE leaderboard runtime past the 300s serverless timeout (FunctionTimeoutError) even though local was fast - caching the handle as static fixed it and the submission then succeeded. WHAT DIDN'T: reduced-precision (prec<3) fails band/rowscale - 3xTF32 is the min; beating geqrf at n=4096 batch=2 (133ms vs 54ms) - only 2 CTAs underutilize. NEXT-BRIEF SUGGESTIONS: (1) MULTI-CTA-per-matrix panel (cooperative-grid or row-split reductions) for small-batch large-n - the panel is now 46.8% of GPU time at n2048 and the only path past geqrf at n4096; (2) cut gather_C/split/form_T overhead (~18% at n2048); (3) recursive (Elmroth-Gustavson) panel to cast panel-internal updates as GEMM. The 'stream' text-scan and cublasCreate-caching findings apply to every custom-CUDA worker.

Inner sub-blocks of bi=smem/(4m) columns each use the fast smem panel kernel; after each, the rest of the panel is updated via compact-WY GEMMs. Replaces the slow single-CTA global panel for large-n. PASSES all 19. 4242->4212us=10.61x. shape5 28210->26821. shape6 unchanged (still geqrf fallback: with two-level my kernel is 77ms vs geqrf 54ms - batch=2 keeps the panel 2-CTA-bound, only multi-CTA would beat geqrf there).

BEST: SHA de5e3b01b556c43bfb479c9b04b79f1099fffb3c, geomean 4212us = 10.61x (was 5121us/8.73x at f293044). BELOW the 4500 target, into the rank 2-7 band (3467-4498). 5 validated wins, all PASS 19 shapes, all leaderboard-safe (no 'stream' text, static cuBLAS handle, 3xTF32 retained where needed): (1) removed gather_C - read C in-place from H via a new split_strided_kernel; (2) split V once/panel, reuse via preA/preB; (3) W=V^TC single TF32 (reads C in-place natively, no split) - BIG win 4868->4374; (4) S=V^TV single TF32 (T factor tolerates it) 4374->4242; (5) two-level blocking for tall panels (m*b>smem) replacing the slow global panel, helped shape5. Per-shape speedups now: s0=4.5,s1=27.8,s2=28,s3=73.7,s4=20.4,s5=2.88,s6=1.0. PRECISION FLOOR found: W,S tolerate single TF32; Y=T^TW and final C-=VY MUST be 3xTF32 (2x or 1x there FAIL band/clustered tests). LEVER 1 (multi-CTA panel) NOT LANDED: I built a full cooperative multi-CTA-per-matrix panel (hand-rolled grid barrier - cg::grid.sync needs -rdc which load_inline can't device-link; my monotonic atomic barrier is PROVEN correct standalone at P=128/600 rounds). It's CORRECT for <=2 concurrent CTAs (P=2 batch=1 rock-solid) and single-panel standalone is correct even at 4 CTAs, but in the REAL multi-panel kernel it corrupts the trailing update whenever >=3-4 CTAs run concurrently at n>=2048 (P>=3 batch=1, OR P=2 batch>=2). b=1 (no within-panel update) always works -> bug is in the multi-CTA within-panel trailing dot/apply, NOT the column factorization (norm/tau verified identical across CTAs via printf). deviceSync makes it deterministic-but-still-wrong, so it's a genuine cross-CTA hazard the threadfences/volatile don't fix, specific to multi-panel+concurrency. The infra is committed but gated OFF (QR_COOP=0, P capped at 2). Shapes 5 (2.88x) and 6 (1.0x, still geqrf - my kernel 77ms vs geqrf 54ms) are the remaining anchors; both need a WORKING multi-CTA panel to fill the 148 SMs at small batch. SUGGESTED NEXT BRIEF: either (a) root-cause the multi-CTA hazard with cuda-memcheck --tool racecheck on the coop kernel inside the multi-panel loop, or (b) try a launch-per-step (non-cooperative, kernel-boundary = implicit grid barrier) multi-CTA panel that's correct-by-construction, or (c) smem-padding the panel kernel to cut bank conflicts (panel is now 49-65% of shapes 3/5).

THE BRIEF'S CORE QUESTIONS, ANSWERED WITH MEASUREMENTS:
1. (H,tau) EMISSION (the known-hard part): SOLVED via orhr_col Modified-LU reconstruction (Ballard et al. 2014). H=triu(S@R)+tril(Y,-1), tau=diag(T=-U diag(S) Y1^-T). Backward-stable for ANY conditioning (LU on the orthonormal Q, NOT the Gram -- so unlike CholeskyQR it passes rankdef/clustered/nearcollinear/band with huge margin: orth<=1.76/gate100, factor<=0.089/gate20). The RECON TAX is SMALL: ~300us/panel (diag_modlu kernel + cuBLAS trsm for L21), << the factorization.
2. ROW-BLOCK FACTORIZATION beats the serial chain: a fused block_qr_Q kernel (one CTA per row-block, forms Q+R in smem) is 21x faster than cuSOLVER linalg.qr on the SM-starved shape5 panel (418us vs 8776us). The brief's central hypothesis is TRUE at the panel level.
3. MERGE STRUCTURE: binary tree (small 2bxb nodes) is the winner. Flat 1-level reduction (Pb x b, one big QR) is SLOWER (4086 vs 2245us) -- occupancy-starved + long serial chain on few CTAs. A fused single-CTA sequential merge is both WRONG (Q-tracking) and slower. b=64 is FORCED (b=128 overflows the 228KB smem ceiling at the 2bxb node); P=8 base, grown adaptively for large m to keep leaf smem under ceiling.
4. THE TRANSFORMATIVE FIX was the TRAILING UPDATE: cuSOLVER ormqr (serial reflector apply) was catastrophic (~198000us/call-batch shape5, the LARGEST cost). Replaced with the compact-WY update C-V T^T(V^T C) = 3 tensor-core cuBLAS GEMMs reusing diag_modlu's T -> 974us->270us. THIS dropped geomean 140194->13300us (10.5x) and crossed below baseline.
